newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy treasury gives details on STET/Telecom share.
newsitem.headline: Italy treasury gives details on STET/Telecom share.

text.p: Italy's treasury said on Friday that savings shares in telecoms holding STET and operator Telecom Italia SpA, which are set to be merged and privatised, would not be converted into ordinary shares.
It said in a statement that a privatisation committee within the treasury had decided that "the conversion of savings shares in STET and Telecom Italia into ordinary shares is not planned."
The committee was aided in its decision by advising banks Morgan Stanley and Euromobiliare as well as global coordinators Bzw and Mediobanca, the statement said.
STET is expected to be privatised in the second half of this year after its merger with Telecom Italia is complete.
The company created by the merger will keep the name Telecom Italia and will become operational on July 18. Its shares will start trading the next day.
Last March, Telecom said that shareholders who do not wish to keep their shares for the merger will be offered 3,938.25 lire per ordinary share and 3,176.59 lire per savings share.
Shareholders in STET who do not want to keep their shares for the merger will be offered 6,466.18 lire per ordinary and 4,976.60 lire per savings share, STET said.
